subject: without any significant effect but higher beta values

messages.author: bdc8dc43cc0e4e82
messages.subject: without any significant effect but higher beta values
parts:
Hi there,


I do appreciate if someone kindly helps me that what's the problem with my analysis.

I'm doing SEM with the lavaan package, two variables considered as a composite variable (as a nonlinear effect). model fit statistics have no problem, but even though beta values for some of the effects are high (0.93, 0.77), but not significant effect for none of them. how can I solve this problem? 

R codes as follows:


########### Model 2.2

m2.2<-' # regressions

B~Score

Score~COMP

B~COMP

DIS~1*D+D^2

soil~1*soilPC1+soilP^2

# composite variable

COMP=~1*S+C

DIS=~B

DIS=~COMP 

DIS=~Score

soil=~B

soil=~COMP 

soil=~Score

# covariance ~~

S~~C

# variances 

DIS~~0*DIS

soil~~0*soil

C~~0.1*C

'


fit1<-lavaan(m2.2,data=Dataset,auto.var=TRUE,test="bollen.stine",se="bootstrap")

f2.2<-fitMeasures(fit1,c("pvalue","rmsea","gfi","cfi", "aic","bic","bic2","chisq", "df"))

f2.2<-inspect(fit1,"rsquare")

f2.2<-parameterEstimates(fit1,standardized=TRUE)


Thanks in advance.
Best Regards,
Anvar,

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: without any significant effect but higher beta values
parts:
It's not necessarily a problem. You have high standard errors. These are correct - although it would be nice to be smaller, I don't think you should think of this as "a problem" to solve.

Increasing your sample size (all else being equal) will shrink your standard errors. (Quadruple your sample to halve your standard errors).

High standard errors also happen because of collinearity - your predictor variables are highly correlated. One solution is to remove a variable, another is to combine them (if they're highly correlated, they're tell your the same thing).
